correctness.rationale: For m>=3 the two essential poles in K2m are separated by two graph edges and every cycle has >=4 edges, so the Abrams unordered two-particle cubical model is a deformation retract by Prue-Scrimshaw sufficient-subdivision conditions. Its c0=binom(m+2,2), c1=2m², c2=m(m-1), with all squares s_ij=(a_i,b_j), i != j. Each q_ji=(b_j,w_i) is a unique free 1-face of s_ij, so collapsing all squares yields a graph homotopy equivalent to subdivided K_(m+1) plus m leaves; cycle rank binom(m,2) for all m. Explicit triangle cycles z_ij=p_ji-p_ij+y_j-y_i form a primitive Z-basis; arm reindexing acts as wedge^2 Z^m. Pole swap sends p_ij to -q_ij and y_i to -x_i, and square boundary q_ji=y_j+x_i-p_ij gives tau[z_ij]=-[z_ij]. Hence the claimed integral S_m x C2 module and character hold universally; independent exact free-square counts and rank checks verified m=3..8.
